title: Petrichor
subtitle: The smell after rain
content: Petrichor is the earthy scent produced when rain falls on dry soil, especially after a period of warm, dry weather.
description: The word was coined by Australian researchers in 1964 from Greek roots related to stone and the fluid believed to flow through the veins of the gods.

title: Susurrus
subtitle: A soft murmuring sound
content: Susurrus means a whispering, murmuring, or rustling sound, such as leaves moving in a breeze.
description: The English word comes from Latin susurrus, meaning a whisper or murmur.

title: Three hearts
subtitle: A remarkable octopus adaptation
content: An octopus has three hearts: two pump blood to the gills, while the third pumps blood to the rest of the body.
description: The heart that supplies the body stops beating while the octopus swims, which helps explain why many octopuses prefer crawling.

title: Honey does not spoil
subtitle: A remarkably stable food
content: Properly stored honey can remain edible for a very long time because its low water content and acidity make it difficult for many microbes to grow.
description: Crystallized honey has not necessarily spoiled; gentle warming can return it to a liquid state.

title: New Zealand
subtitle: Aotearoa in the southwestern Pacific
content: New Zealand is an island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean. Its capital city is Wellington, while Auckland is its largest urban area.
description: The country consists primarily of the North Island and South Island, along with many smaller islands.

title: Iceland
subtitle: An island shaped by fire and ice
content: Iceland is an island country in the North Atlantic known for volcanoes, glaciers, geothermal areas, and a capital city called Reykjavik.
description: Its location on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge helps explain its active geology and abundant geothermal energy.

title: Axolotl
subtitle: A salamander that keeps its juvenile form
content: The axolotl is a salamander that normally retains larval features, including external gills, throughout its life in water.
description: Axolotls are native to the lake complex around Mexico City and are well known for their ability to regenerate some body tissues.

title: Tardigrade
subtitle: The water bear
content: Tardigrades are microscopic animals that can enter a dehydrated state called a tun, allowing some species to survive harsh conditions.
description: Their resilience does not make them indestructible, but their ability to pause much of their metabolism is extraordinary.

title: Why the sky looks blue
subtitle: Light scattered through air
content: The daytime sky looks blue because molecules in Earth's atmosphere scatter shorter blue wavelengths of sunlight more strongly than longer red wavelengths.
description: At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, so scattered light can make the sky appear orange or red.

title: The water cycle
subtitle: Earth's continuous movement of water
content: Water moves continuously through evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration, runoff, and collection in Earth's water cycle.
description: The cycle is powered mainly by solar energy and gravity and links oceans, atmosphere, land, and living systems.

title: Sagittarius A*
subtitle: The black hole at the Milky Way's center
content: Sagittarius A* is the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way galaxy, about 26,000 light-years from Earth.
description: Astronomers study the motion of nearby stars and other observations to understand this compact object.

title: The Pillars of Creation
subtitle: A star-forming region in the Eagle Nebula
content: The Pillars of Creation are towering columns of gas and dust in the Eagle Nebula where new stars form and ultraviolet light shapes the surrounding material.
description: The region is roughly 6,500 light-years away and became widely known through images from the Hubble Space Telescope.

title: The first Moon landing
subtitle: Apollo 11 reached the lunar surface in 1969
content: On July 20, 1969, NASA's Apollo 11 lunar module landed on the Moon, and Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin later walked on its surface.
description: Michael Collins remained in lunar orbit in the command module while the landing crew worked on the surface.

title: The Rosetta Stone
subtitle: A key to reading Egyptian hieroglyphs
content: The Rosetta Stone carries the same decree in hieroglyphic, Demotic, and ancient Greek scripts, helping scholars decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs.
description: The stone was discovered in 1799 during Napoleon's campaign in Egypt and is now held by the British Museum.

title: Machu Picchu
subtitle: An Inca site in the Andes
content: Machu Picchu is a fifteenth-century Inca citadel located high in the Andes of Peru, above the Urubamba Valley.
description: Its terraces, plazas, and stone structures form part of a UNESCO World Heritage site.

title: The Great Barrier Reef
subtitle: The world's largest coral reef ecosystem
content: The Great Barrier Reef is a vast coral reef ecosystem off the northeastern coast of Australia, made up of thousands of reefs and hundreds of islands.
description: It supports diverse marine life and is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site.
source_name: Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority
